app.name: Jaipur Studio Ceramics Shop
app.summary: A small online shop for a Jaipur ceramics maker who sells mugs, bowls, planters and vases in batches of ten or twenty. Buyers browse what is actually in stock, choose a glaze and size, and place an order for studio pickup in Jaipur or courier delivery, paying the maker later by UPI. The maker signs in to manage pieces and stock, create discount codes, see new orders, track who has paid, and mark orders packed, shipped or collected.
app.audience: A solo ceramic maker in Jaipur selling small-batch pieces, and buyers in Jaipur and elsewhere in India who want to buy those pieces without messaging on Instagram.

roles.name: Shop Owner
roles.description: The ceramic maker. Signs in to manage pieces, glaze and size variants and stock, create discount codes, maintain the studio pickup details, and work through orders: mark UPI payment received, packed, shipped or collected, or cancel an order. This is the role the app exists to serve.

roles.name: Buyer
roles.description: A person buying ceramics. Never signs in. Browses the public shop, sees honest stock per glaze and size, chooses studio pickup or courier, optionally uses a discount code, and places an order, paying the maker later by UPI.

vocabulary.description: One ceramic design for sale, such as a mug, shown with photos so buyers can judge it without messaging the maker.
One purchasable combination of glaze and size for a piece, with its own price adjustment if any and its own stock count. Stock, sold-out and nearly-gone states are tracked per Variant.

A buyer's placed order, received by the shop owner. Fields: buyer name, phone, fulfilment (Studio Pickup or Courier), delivery address for courier orders, discount code used, piece total, discount amount, shipping charge, final total, placed date and time. Order status: New, Packed, Shipped, Collected, Cancelled. Payment status: Awaiting UPI Payment, Paid.
One line of an order: the piece, its chosen glaze and size, quantity ordered and the price at the time of ordering. Quantity cannot exceed the variant stock at the time the order is placed.
A code word the owner shares, for example on Instagram for a weekend, that buyers enter at checkout. Fields: code word, discount value, start date, end date, and active or deactivated state.
The owner's shop details shown to buyers: shop name, studio pickup address and pickup instructions.

capabilities.note: Only the shop owner signs up and signs in with email and password to manage the shop; buyers order without an account.
The signed-in shop owner sees and manages only their own pieces, variants, discount codes and orders.

The owner can list, view, create, edit and delete pieces, glaze and size variants and discount codes, and can view and update orders. Deleting a piece removes it and its variants from the public shop but does not delete past orders that contain it.
Buyers can filter the public shop by piece type (Mug, Bowl, Planter, Vase) and by availability, and sort by price; the owner can filter orders by status and payment status.
Two roles only: the signed-in shop owner and the guest buyer who never signs in.
A public landing page that is also the shop front, plus public read-only piece pages showing photos, price, glaze and size options and honest remaining stock.

Order status moves New to Packed, then Packed to Shipped for courier orders or Packed to Collected for pickup orders; the owner may move a New or Packed order to Cancelled. Payment status moves separately from Awaiting UPI Payment to Paid when the owner confirms UPI collection.
Each piece has one type used as its category: Mug, Bowl, Planter or Vase.
Orders record the date and time placed; discount codes have a start and end date so a weekend code expires automatically.

The shop shows pieces remaining per variant and sold-out state; the owner sees counts of new orders, orders awaiting payment, and variants that are nearly gone, plus order totals including discount and shipping.
The owner maintains the shop name, studio pickup address and pickup instructions shown to buyers.
Simulated: the owner can add piece photos through a full upload UI; each file is validated and previewed and kept for the session, and nothing is stored.
Mentioned in the idea but deliberately left out: no online payment is taken; the owner collects by UPI outside the app and marks the order Paid.
Mentioned in the idea but left out: no Instagram or courier integration; codes are posted to Instagram by hand and couriers are arranged by hand.

inScope: A public landing page that is the shop front: it says this is the Jaipur studio's own shop for small-batch mugs, bowls, planters and vases, shows the pieces for sale, and invites buyers to browse and order without messaging the maker. The shop owner signs in from this page.

Buyers browse pieces with photos doing the talking: each piece shows its type (Mug, Bowl, Planter or Vase), price, description, available glazes and sizes, how many are left per glaze and size, and a clear sold-out state when none are left. A variant with 0 left cannot be ordered.

A buyer chooses a piece, a glaze and a size, and a quantity no greater than the stock remaining for that variant, then places an order without creating an account. A new buyer can go from the landing page to a visible order confirmation in five steps or fewer, and the confirmation is still there after a refresh.

At checkout the buyer chooses Studio Pickup (Jaipur only, always free) or Courier. Courier costs ₹99, and nothing above ₹1,500: courier orders with a total above ₹1,500 after discount get free shipping. The buyer sees the piece total, discount, shipping and final total before confirming.

No online payment is taken. Placing an order creates it with payment status Awaiting UPI Payment, and the confirmation tells the buyer the maker will collect payment by UPI later. Stock is reduced as soon as the order is placed so the shop stays honest about what is left and a glaze cannot be oversold.

Buyers can enter one discount code per order at checkout. A valid code reduces the order total; an invalid, expired or deactivated code is rejected with a message and the buyer can continue without it.

The shop owner signs in and manages the catalogue: create, edit and delete pieces, set each piece's type, price, description and photos, and set its glaze and size variants with a stock count for each variant (typically a batch of ten or twenty).
The shop owner creates and deactivates discount codes with a code word, a discount value, and start and end dates, for example for a weekend promotion shared on Instagram.

The shop owner sees a list of orders, newest first, with buyer name and phone, pickup or courier choice and address where relevant, items with glaze and size, totals, order status and payment status. The owner marks an order Paid when UPI payment is collected, and moves orders from New to Packed, then to Shipped for courier orders or Collected for pickup orders; the owner can cancel a New or Packed order, which returns its stock.

The shop owner sees which glaze and size variants are nearly gone (2 or fewer left) and which are sold out, so they can plan the next batch, and sees simple counts of new orders and orders still awaiting UPI payment.

Business rules: there is one shop owner and one shop; buyers never sign in; a piece is available only while at least one of its variants has stock; an order cannot exceed the stock of the chosen variant; deleting a piece removes it and its variants from the public shop but never deletes past orders.

outOfScope.item: Online payments, including in-app UPI collection and card payments
outOfScope.reason: The maker explicitly does not want to set up online payments yet and collects by UPI later.
outOfScope.placeholder: Checkout completes without payment, the order is marked Awaiting UPI Payment, the confirmation says the maker will collect by UPI later, and the owner marks it Paid once collected outside the app.

outOfScope.item: Buyer accounts and buyer order history
outOfScope.reason: The idea asks buyers to order without messaging the maker and never asks buyers to sign in; guest checkout keeps ordering to as few steps and fields as possible.
outOfScope.placeholder: Buyers order as guests and get an on-screen order confirmation that remains visible after a refresh in the same session; questions about an order go to the maker using the phone number given at checkout.

outOfScope.item: Courier booking, courier tracking and shipping labels
outOfScope.reason: The idea only requires a courier option with a flat ₹99 charge and free shipping above ₹1,500, not a courier service connection.
outOfScope.placeholder: The delivery address is shown as text on the order, the owner arranges the courier outside the app, and marks the order Shipped by hand.

outOfScope.item: Instagram integration, including posting discount codes or importing Instagram enquiries
outOfScope.reason: The idea mentions Instagram only as where codes are announced and as the old sales channel being replaced.
outOfScope.placeholder: The owner creates a discount code in the shop and posts the same code word on Instagram by hand; buyers type it in at checkout.

assumptions.text: Placing an order immediately reduces the stock of the chosen glaze and size variant, so the public shop never promises stock that has already been ordered. If the shop owner cancels an order, its stock is returned to the variant.
A glaze and size variant counts as nearly gone when 2 or fewer pieces remain, and as sold out when 0 remain. The owner can plan the next batch from a low-stock list using this default threshold.

The ₹99 courier charge and free shipping above ₹1,500 are calculated on the order total after any discount is applied. Studio pickup is always free. Courier orders at or below ₹1,500 pay ₹99; courier orders above ₹1,500 pay no shipping.

A buyer does not create an account. To place an order the buyer must give a name, phone number, and, for courier orders only, a delivery address; pickup orders do not require a delivery address. The buyer sees the order confirmation on screen and it remains visible after a refresh in the same session.

The studio pickup address and pickup instructions are shown as text on the shop and on the order confirmation. Courier orders are marked Shipped when the maker hands them to a courier arranged outside the app.

A buyer can use at most one discount code per order. A code stops working after its end date or when the owner deactivates it, and an invalid, expired or deactivated code is rejected at checkout with a message and a way to continue without it.
Buyers cannot cancel or edit an order themselves in the MVP. Only the shop owner can cancel an order, which returns its stock and keeps the order visible in the owner's order list as Cancelled.

questions.question: Should a discount code take a percentage off the order or a fixed ₹ amount off?
questions.whyItMatters: It changes the DiscountCode data, the checkout calculation and the shipping threshold check.
questions.defaultAnswer: The owner chooses per code between a percentage off and a fixed ₹ amount off, with one code allowed per order.

questions.question: Is free shipping based on the order total after discount, and does exactly ₹1,500 qualify?
questions.whyItMatters: It changes the order total buyers see and the amount the maker collects by UPI.
questions.defaultAnswer: Free shipping applies when the courier order total after discount is above ₹1,500; at exactly ₹1,500 the ₹99 charge still applies.

questions.question: How many pieces left should count as nearly gone for planning the next batch?
questions.whyItMatters: It changes the low-stock list the owner relies on, but a default of 2 is safe for batches of ten or twenty.
questions.defaultAnswer: Nearly gone means 2 or fewer pieces left for that glaze and size variant.

questions.question: Should pickup be restricted to buyers in Jaipur, and are pickup times scheduled in the app?
questions.whyItMatters: Restricting pickup or adding time slots would change checkout fields and order data; the default keeps checkout short.
questions.defaultAnswer: Studio pickup is offered to every buyer at checkout, with the studio address and pickup instructions shown as text; the buyer arranges the pickup time with the maker by phone.
